title: Renewal thresholds & escalation decision tree — QBR-ready playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, QBR-friendly playbook that maps measurable renewal thresholds to a decision tree and a set of mitigations/save plays. Intended as a working doc for CSMs and their managers during QBRs, renewal windows, and triage huddles. Draft — contains practical scripts, a checklist, and TODOs for automation.

Scope:
- Target: mid-market and enterprise accounts with >$50k ARR
- Time window: 90 days before renewal to 30 days after renewal date (if still open)
- Owners: CSM (primary), AM/AE (commercial contact), Support Eng (technical), CSM Manager (escalation), CRO/Head of CS (exec escalation)

Quick summary (one-liner):
Map usage + health signals -> threshold bucket (green/yellow/red) -> apply prescribed mitigation(s) -> escalate according to decision tree.

Core signals to evaluate in QBR (metrics we check every QBR / renewal check):
- Product usage: active seats, DAU/WAU, top feature adoption (list features)
- Request volume to support and time-to-resolution (avg P1/P2 SLA adherence)
- Business metrics: value milestones hit (integrations, go-live, revenue lift)
- Financial signals: spend trend (MoM change), overage incidents, invoicing disputes
- Sentiment: NPS/CSAT trends, QBR feedback notes, product complaints logged
- Risk signals: open P1s >72h, unpaid invoices >30d, exec churn signals (departure of champion)

Threshold buckets (numeric examples — adapt per account sizing):
- Green (low risk): usage >= 70% of committed seats OR growth MoM >= +5%, NPS >= 30, no P1 >24h, invoices current. Action: standard QBR cadence, prepare renewal offer 90d out.
- Yellow (moderate risk): usage between 40%–69% OR flat/decline MoM between -5% and +4%, NPS between 10–29 OR 1 P1 >24h but <72h, minor billing issues. Action: targeted mitigation plays, CSM manager notified, prioritized play deployment 60–45d out.
- Red (high risk): usage <40% OR MoM decline <= -5%, NPS <10 OR P1s >72h OR invoices >30d OR champion left. Action: immediate save play, commercial/exec escalation, 30–0d push for retention.

Decision tree (stepwise guidance used during QBR or renewal triage):
1) Collect signals (see Core signals) and populate the Renewal Risk Row in the tracker.
2) Assign preliminary bucket (green/yellow/red) based on majority of signals. 
3) If any single hard trigger exists (unpaid invoice >30d, open P1 >72h, champion departure), forcibly escalate to Red and tag for exec attention.
4) For Yellow: run targeted mitigation plays (see "Mitigation playbook") and set 2-week check-ins. CSM Manager reviews progress at 7 days. If no measurable lift in two cycles -> escalate to Red.
5) For Red: open a cross-functional war room (CS, AE, Support Eng, Finance). Draft a tailored save play within 48 hours and present to CRO/Head of CS for exec sign-off.
6) If save play fails to produce contract renewal intent by -7 days, prepare attrition brief for leadership and set furlough/hand-off plan.

Escalation matrix (roles, triggers, actions):
- CSM (first responder): compiles signals, owns mitigation plays, daily check-ins for Red customers. Templates: outreach email, meeting agenda.
- CSM Manager: notified when status >= Yellow or on any hard trigger. Reviews mitigation, approves budgets for discounts/credits.
- AE/AM: engaged when commercial concessions or upsell/deferral discussions required. Must own offer terms.
- Support Eng / Solutions: engaged when technical blockers prevent value. Provide patch timeline or workaround within 48 hrs.
- Finance: engaged when invoicing/billing is the trigger. Prioritize dispute resolution.
- Head of CS / CRO: engaged on exec escalation for Red (must happen within 72 hrs of escalation).

Mitigation playbook (catalog of plays with short scripts and success criteria):
- "Usage Reboot": 1) 30–60 min workshop with power users + solutions engineer; 2) create 30-day action plan around top 3 features; 3) success criteria: 20% feature usage lift or commitment to pilot new workflow.
- "Technical Rapid Response": triage P1, deliver hotfix/workaround in 48 hrs, daily status to customer + internal war room. Success: P1 resolved or accepted workaround and timeline agreed.
- "Commercial Reconnect": AE offers limited-time credit or term adjustment (approved by CSM Manager). Template offer in Templates section. Success: signed amendment or LOI to continue.
- "Exec Alignment Call": 30-min call between customer exec and CS/CRO to reestablish value and roadmap alignment. Pre-read: 1-pager business outcomes + open risk items. Success: exec re-commitment or clear exit plan.
- "Pilot Expansion": propose a short, low-risk pilot of a new use-case with clear KPIs and fixed budget. Success: pilot converted into paid expansion or explicit rationale for closure.

Save plays (email and call scripts — pick and adapt):
- Outreach subject: "Critical: plan to secure [Customer]’s value from Redwood — request 30 minutes"
- Email body (short): "Hi [Champion], we ran the numbers and see adoption slipping in X area. We'd like 30 mins to present a focused plan (workshop + timeline + proposed concession) to get you back to value. Are you available [two slots]? — Maya (CSM)"
- Call script bullets: lead with 1) top positive outcome from onboarding; 2) present gap (data-backed); 3) offer 2 concrete mitigations (workshop or credit); 4) ask for commitment (date to decide).

QBR slide prompts to include when preparing renewal-focused QBR (one slide each):
- Health snapshot: 3 charts (usage, support volume, NPS trend) + one-sentence interpretation.
- Value milestones: achieved / at-risk / committed next 90 days.
- Risk assessment: threshold bucket + top 3 root causes.
- Proposed remedies: prioritized playbook actions + owner + ETA.
- Commercial ask: renewal recommendation and proposed structure (standard / discount / pilot)
- Executive notes: anything that needs leadership time.

Tracker fields (what CSMs should keep updated in renewal tracker row):
- renewal_date, current_status_bucket, last_quarter_usage_pct, support_P1_count, open_billing_issues, champion_status (active/inactive), mitigation_play_active (Y/N), next_checkin_date, exec_escalation_needed (Y/N), notes.

Success criteria and measurement (short list):
- Immediate: mitigate P1s, close billing disputes, and demonstrate 10–20% short-term usage improvement within 30 days.
- Midterm: customer signs renewal or pilot extension, or provides documented proof of decision to exit.
- Outcome: closed-won renewal or documented handoff for churn.

Operational notes / automation TODOs (things to build into tracker or Slack alerts):
- Auto-flag accounts with 2 consecutive months of usage decline >5%
- Slack alert to #cs-escalations on unpaid invoice >30d with account link and ARR
- Weekly feed of top 20 at-risk accounts into QBR prep doc for CSM managers
- Template generation for save-play emails + meeting agendas from tracker data

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to leadership):
- How deep should commercial concessions be allowed at manager level vs. CRO approval? (proposed: manager can approve up to 10% ARR credit; >10% requires CRO)
- Should we standardize numeric thresholds by ARR band? (recommended yes — next step: define bands)
- Where to store final exec briefing: Confluence exec-briefs vs. private drive folder?

Immediate action items (owner):
- Maya: prototype tracker row template and share with CSM managers (due 2026-02-19)
- Diego: add Slack alert pipeline for unpaid invoices and P1 age (due 2026-03-05)
- Priya: draft standard offer templates for manager-level concessions (due 2026-02-26)

Appendix (quick links and examples):
- Example email template: (see Save plays section)
- Example Jira ticket tags to use when opening "renewal-risk" issues: CS-RENEWAL-xxx
- Confluence draft: renewal playbook (linked above)

Notes to self: this is intentionally concise for QBR slide conversion. We should later expand with specific ARR bands and pre-approved concession matrix. Keep this doc as the canonical QBR decision tree for CS triage meetings.

Revision log (simple):
- 2025-09-10: initial draft (Maya)
- 2026-01-14: added threshold buckets and mitigation catalog (team input)
- 2026-02-12: updated escalation timing and action owners (in review)
